SoM marker v5 — the paper's method

Set-of-Mark (arXiv 2310.11441) marks regions, and its regions come from a segmenter. Our answers are points, so a mark's region is the SAM segment at that point — the same way the paper obtains its regions. Everything else is taken from the paper and microsoft/SoM's visualizer.py: translucent overlay at alpha 0.4 (the paper's COCO GT value), a contour in the mark colour, and the number placed at the distance-transform maximum inside the region — the pixel furthest from any boundary — with the visualizer's (+2, −6) offset and its font-size rule clip((h_ratio−0.02)/0.08+1, 1.2, 2) × 0.5 × base. Regions are placed smallest-first with occupied spots excluded, and a region too small to hold its number has the number moved off it, as the paper prescribes.

Earlier versions (v2/v3/v4) drew an opaque ring on the judged point and a filled badge beside it. Neither element exists in the paper; the ring was the source of the occlusion.

Left = v3 (current data)  |  Right = v5 (paper method).
